independent.summary: `newUserHandle`'s doc comment says "Also the schema default, so every account created has one (models/User.js)" and `routes/auth.js:339` repeats "Every account created since carries one from the schema default" — but there is deliberately no schema `default`; `User.js` uses a `pre('validate')` hook guarded on `isNew` precisely because a default would also fire on hydration, and the Decision Log entry documents that as the key decision. The comments contradict the mechanism they describe and invite a future change to "simplify" the hook into the default the code explicitly rejects.

grades.reason: An empty/complete list is the intended semantics — the ids come straight from the server's own answer, and when the server holds no passkeys the authenticator *should* drop them all (scoped to rpId+this account's handle), so there is no scenario where a partial or bogus list is passed; the only non-array case is already guarded by `Array.isArray`.

The claim is untrue: `passkeys.test.js` asserts the stored handle directly via `storedHandle()` (43-char base64url, 32 bytes, non-identifying), that two `register/begin` calls answer that same stored value, that two accounts differ, that the backfill is written once under a race, and that the list route returns it — line 659 is the removal test, which additionally compares the response's `userHandle` to the stored one.

triageGrades.reason: The change rewrites WebAuthn registration options, the passkey sign-in failure path, and the passkey list/remove routes — squarely authentication.
No new secrets, env vars, or credential material handling; the user handle is a non-secret random account identifier that WebAuthn puts in the credential anyway, and no public key is exposed.
Nothing touches billing, budgets, or model-cost paths.

The change newly asks an authenticator to erase credentials it holds (`signalAllAcceptedCredentials` drops anything not in the list, `signalUnknownCredential` forgets one) — irreversible state outside the DB; the cited line is weak evidence but the category is genuinely touched.

It adds calls into the browser's WebAuthn Signal API — an out-of-app surface that may be absent or throw, handled with feature detection and swallowed errors; evidence line is weak (an import line) but the category applies.
No version bump, deploy config, or migration — the backfill is deliberately lazy so nothing has to be run against production.

summary: Both findings are false positives built on premises the code contradicts (the id list comes from the server and an empty list is the intended signal; the handle's storage, stability and uniqueness are each asserted by dedicated tests), while the triage calls are all right; the only thing of substance in this well-tested change — two comments asserting a schema `default` the design explicitly rejects — was missed.
